summary: Guidance for shadow-traffic migration + snapshot rollback after aggressive batch/quant profile change causing intermittent 95p latency increases
description:
Issue summary:
Customer applied a tenant-scoped optimizer profile that enabled aggressive async-batching, KV prefetch and an 8-bit quantization profile. After rollout, they report intermittent 95th percentile latency spikes (~200-400ms above baseline) and occasional streaming partial frames (client sees chunk gaps) for production traffic.

Impact:
- Affects NeonMed's dedicated cluster (single reserved pool) in us-east-1.
- Approximately 12% of requests observed above customer SLA target at 95p during peak.
- User-facing degradations for key interactive endpoint (chat/stream).

Environment:
- Deployment: Dedicated (reserved) pool, tenant NeonMed, 4x A100-equivalent instances
- Runtime version: serving-runtime v2.9.1
- Optimizer profile: tenant/optimizers/neonmed-aggressive-v2 (enabled 2026-03-09 14:20 UTC)
- Traffic pattern: bursty short-turn conversations (mean tokens 80, tail to 1024), streaming enabled

Steps to reproduce (customer reported):
1) Send multiple concurrent interactive streams (50 concurrent sessions) with mixed short and long contexts.
2) Observe occasional 95p latency spikes and streaming chunk gaps.
3) Reverting manually to the previous optimizer profile appears to reduce spikes but customer needs a safe rollback plan.

Logs & telemetry snippets provided by customer:
- Request traces: https://telemetry.redwood.ai/trace/NEON-20260309-88a
- Console screenshot (percentile graph): https://files.neonmed.com/latency-spike-0309.png

Notes on urgency: Customer is on a dedicated contract and requires resolution or a safe mitigation within 48hrs to meet SLAs for a live product demo on 2026-03-15.
investigation_notes:
Initial analysis (Marcos Silva):
- Correlation seen between optimizer rollout time and first spike window.
- KV prefetch appears to increase memory pressure for longer contexts, causing intermittent GC-like stalls in the runtime thread.
- Async-batching improved throughput but introduced queuing jitter under bursty short sessions.
- Streaming chunk gaps likely due to head-of-line delays when a long request sits in a batch.
- No 5xx spike; errors are primarily increased tail latency and some client perceived stream discontinuities.

Hypotheses tested:
- Disabled KV prefetch for a single backend pod in staging: 95p improved but throughput dropped slightly.
- Reduced max-batch-size from 64 to 32 in a canary: reduced 95p by ~120ms.

Next steps proposed:
1) Advise customer to enable traffic shadowing (split traffic 10% shadow -> new profile, 90% stable) while keeping the aggressive profile in shadow mode to collect telemetry without impacting users.
2) Prepare atomic snapshot of tenant optimizer settings and a fast revert script to restore previous profile per-tenant.
3) Provide stepwise tuning suggestions: lower async batch window, disable KV prefetch for streaming endpoints, and revert quantization to 16-bit fallback for long sequences.
4) Recommend using routing policy to pin streaming endpoints to a less aggressive profile until post-tuning verification.

resolution_notes:
Mitigation in progress as of 2026-03-13:
- Applied conservative changes to streaming routes (async delay reduced, max-batch-size reduced to 32) which improved 95p by ~90-130ms in the canary.
- Enabled 10% shadowing to gather live behavior for the aggressive profile without impacting production.
- Prepared tenant optimizer snapshot and tested per-tenant revert script in staging (PR linked).

If metrics do not stabilize after full tuning steps, plan is to execute per-tenant snapshot revert to previous optimizer profile during the approved maintenance window (2026-03-14 02:00 UTC).

Follow-ups:
- SRE to add a sentinel: auto-detect 95p regression >100ms for 15min and trigger a support alert.
- Support to provide a compact runbook for customers to perform safe shadowing and atomic revert in the Console.
- Engineering to evaluate memory footprint of KV prefetch under long-context workloads and consider a bounded-prefetch mode.
